scores.Rationale: The proposal addresses a significant public health issue regarding Lyme disease misdiagnosis and the critical role of physical therapists as first-line providers. Identifying gaps in PT education and clinical differential diagnosis abilities is a novel and highly relevant area of inquiry, laying crucial groundwork for future interventions.

This section contains major gaps. The timeline for completing the project is entirely missing, severely undermining feasibility. While survey validation is planned, the sampling strategy relies on convenience samples which limits generalizability, and specific details on how diagnostic accuracy will be objectively scored for Aim 2 are insufficient.

The PI is well-qualified, and the Co-Investigators bring complementary and essential expertise in content (PA faculty) and survey design/PT education. Their clearly defined roles and relevant publication records demonstrate a strong fit for the proposed work.

The project clearly aims to generate preliminary data for future interventional studies, which aligns well with competitive grant mechanisms. The explicit identification of the International Lyme and Associated Diseases Educational Foundation (ILADEF) as a potential future funder further strengthens this criterion.

The budget is exceptionally clear, detailed, and well-justified. All expenses are directly tied to proposed activities, appear cost-effective for a seed grant, and demonstrate leveraging of other institutional funds for travel.

The proposal suffers from significant organizational issues. The critical timeline section is completely absent, and large portions of the 'Project' description are duplicated verbatim within the 'Biosketches' section, indicating a severe lack of attention to detail and professional presentation.
